text: A wireless message from Tientsin reports that after heavy artillery fire from the Kuominchun lines this morning at three o'clock they attacked in force the whole line from Hankou village to Meichang, driving Li Ching-lin's forces back to their reserve lines between Peitsang and Hsittow.

label: text
text: The Chihli troops were driven back four or five kilometres, and there are indications that the Chihli defence is breaking down as they are outnumbered by three to one. Feng's troops are expected to reach Tientsin to-morrow or even to-night. However, Li Ching-lin went to the front yesterday afternoon to organise a last stand.

label: text
text: The Japanese Government is sending immediately from Port Arthur two hundred troops to Tientsin, making a total garrison of 550.

label: text
text: It is stated that the situation is rather precarious in the Tientsin district.

label: text
text: The Press publishes the text of the Turco-Soviet Treaty concluded in Paris last Thursday between Mr. Chicherin and Tewfik Rushdid "tending to strengthen the exceptional friendship uniting Turkey and the Soviet," stipulating that if one were attacked, the other will remain neutral in relation to the first.

label: text
text: Each nation undertakes to refrain from attacking the other, and not to participate in any political union or agreement with one or several third parties directed against the other contracting party nor any similar union or agreement directed against the military or naval safety of the other party.

label: text
text: The agreement becomes valid on the ratification for three years of three protocols, which lay down:—

label: text
text: First: Each reserves full freedom of action in relation to other Power's outside the limits and obligations stipulated in the present agreement.

label: text
text: Second: Sets forth the “political nature” of the union or agreement aforementioned which comprises financial or economic agreements between any countries directed against either signatory.

label: text
text: Third: Lays down that the parties agree to arrange parleys to fix the method of arranging possible mutual differences that cannot be adjusted by diplomatic means.

label: text
text: President Coolidge is drawing up a reply to the invitation to the United States to attend a preliminary discussion on disarmaments. It is stated at White House that his study of the question is "of a constructive and affirmative nature."

label: text
text: Senator King Introduced a resolution in the Senate in favour of authorising the United States to participate in the Disarmament Conference.

label: text
text: As the result of a conference between representatives of the Printing Federation and the Newspaper Society, the evening newspapers will be published in most provincial towns on Boxing Day.

label: text
text: The King's Speech at the pro-rogation of Parliament opens with a reference to the death of Queen Alexandra, and acknowledges the sympathy expressed in all parts of the Dominions, and foreign countries.

label: text
text: It expresses pride in the warm welcome given to H.R.H. the Prince of Wales on his recent visit to South Africa, West Africa, and South America.

label: text
text: It believes that the agreements made at Locarno and signed in London will prove not only, the foundation of true peace between the peoples immediately concerned but the beginning of friendly cooperation which cannot fail to benefit the whole world.

label: text
text: It is his heartfelt prayer that the Irish agreement will advance co-operation and strengthen goodwill in Ireland.

label: text
text: Gratitude is expressed to all throughout the Empire who co-operated in the Wembley Exhibition. His Majesty is sure that the increased knowledge which it brought of the resources and activities of his people will have lasting beneficial results.

text: Further preferences, in Empire imports have been made, and other measures for the development of Empire trade are being

label: text
text: The death is reported of Mr. Frank Andrew Munsey, the well-known publisher.

label: text
text: Mr. Munsey, who was born in 1854, started his business career in a country store, and became manager of the Western Union Telegraph Office at Augusta. In 1882 he went to New York and started "The Golden Argosy," a juvenile weekly; in 1889 he started "Munsey's Weekly," which was converted into "Munsey's Magazine" in 1891. He also owned "The Argosy," "All Story Weekly," "New York Mail," "Sun and Globe," and "Evening Telegram." He was the author of five books, the last of which was published as far back as 1894.

label: text
text: Mr. Hoover, with the co-operation of the National Rubber and Automobile Associations, has launched a programme with the slogan "a patch in time saves nine" to arouse the public to economise in rubber, especially in motor tyres, in regard to which a reduction in consumption of 25 per cent is considered feasible.

label: text
text: The League has received the acceptance of the American, Mr. Frederic Delano (who was born in Hongkong) as Chairman of the Opium Commission to Persia.

label: text
text: Mr. Delano, accompanied by his British and French colleagues to Teheran, expects to complete the investigation and report to the Council in June.

label: text
text: Delano will be instructed to ascertain whether Turkey will attempt to cornenthe opium production in the event of Persia abandoning it.

text: Northern Japan was swept by a storm yesterday, the losses reported including twenty fishing boats which capsized. 150 fishermen being missing in the Fukushima Prefecture.

label: text
text: Numbers of houses were destroyed and twenty people are missing at Aomori.

label: text
text: Forty vessels were shipwrecked, with ten casualties, at Muroran.

label: text
text: Ten men and six houses were carried away by a tidal wave at Oshima and Hokkaido, respectively.

label: text
text: Several deaths, casualties, and damage are reported from other parts.

label: text
text: The Federation of Master Cotton Spinners' Associations, at a meeting in Manchester, unanimously decided to recommend a week's stoppage in the American section between December 24 and January 9, excluding the Christmas holidays, in view of the deplorable state of the yarn market in the American section.

label: text
text: Before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning, Lance Sergeant C.E. Taylor of the Hongkong Police was charged on two counts of being drunk and unfit for duty and absenting himself from his station at West Point at 8 p.m. on Monday.

label: text
text: Mr. D. Burlingham (D.S.P.) said that the defendant had served since March 1924 and had been reported by the doctor to be suffering from a disease in the eyes. He was given the option of resigning or going before a medical board. No resignation had been sent in, and apparently failing to get a billet elsewhere, he took to drink and absented himself from duty.

label: text
text: Defendant pleaded guilty to both charges and had no explanation to offer.

label: text
text: Remarking that defendant had a bad record, His Worship imposed a fine of $50, or three weeks' hard labour, on each charge.

text:
RICSHA PULLER WHO
BOLTED
JAILED ON TWO CHARGES
A riccha coolie was charged at the Central Magistracy this morning with the theft of a letter case and alternatively with falling to report the find to the police.

label: text
text:
The evidence was that a Chinese merchant inadvertently left the letter case containing banking documents in the ricaha at the Bank of Canton building. On discovering his loss the merchant ran back to find the ricaha coolie, but he had disappeared. He was arrested later by the police and reluctantly surrendered the missing article.
Defendant was sentenced to undergo one month's hard labour on the first charge and fourteen days on the other, the sentences to run concurrently
